**Date:** 2025-04-26
**Time:** 14:17 PST
**Agent:** Lisa Wang (agent_005) - Sales Specialist, Experience Level: 0.6
**Customer:** Customer ID: C00077940 (29yo, Middle income)

---

**(Call Connects - Faint background noise on customer's end)**

**Lisa Wang:** Thank you for calling TriLink Telecom, my name is Lisa, how can I help you today?

**Customer:** Yeah, hi Lisa. Um, I need some help with my bill. My latest one just came in, and it's… it's really high. I think I need to set up a payment arrangement or something.

**Lisa Wang:** Okay, no problem, I can certainly check into that for you. To start, could you please verify your full name and the phone number associated with your account?

**Customer:** Sure. It's Alex Chen, and the number is 555-876-4321.

**Lisa Wang:** Thank you, Alex. And just for security, could you confirm your date of birth, please?

**Customer:** March 15th, 1996.

**Lisa Wang:** Perfect, thank you. Just a moment while I pull up your account... Okay, I see your account here, C00077940. Your current services are the Standard_100 Internet plan at $74 a month, and the Limited_10GB mobile plan with two lines for $99 a month. Is that all correct?

**Customer:** Yeah, that's right. And my bill's $173, right?

**Lisa Wang:** That's correct, your total due for this billing cycle is $173.00, and the due date is May 1st.

**Customer:** Right. Look, I'm just… I'm having a bit of a tough time this month, and honestly, with how unreliable my service has been, it just feels like a lot to pay all at once. Is there any way I can split this up, like pay half now and half in a couple weeks?

**Lisa Wang:** I understand, Alex. Let me see what options are available on my end. (Typing sounds) Hmm, okay. So, Alex, as a sales specialist, my primary focus is usually on optimizing your plans or exploring new offers to ensure you're getting the best value. Payment arrangements are generally handled by our billing department.

**Customer:** Well, can you transfer me then? Or can you just see if there's *anything* you can do? Because I'm getting really fed up with TriLink, honestly. My internet's always slowing down – I mean, I pay for 100 Mbps, but it feels like 20 most days. And with that, my mobile data just eats up my allowance because I'm always switching to it when the Wi-Fi acts up. I've had so many overage charges, I've had so many outages... it's just getting ridiculous.

**Lisa Wang:** I hear your frustration, Alex, and I sincerely apologize for the issues you've been experiencing with your service. I see a high number of recent speed complaints and some reported outages on your internet service, as well as several mobile data overage charges. (Hesitates slightly) While I can certainly look into those service issues for you – perhaps schedule a technician visit for the internet – regarding a payment arrangement specifically for the current bill, my system is showing limited options.

**Customer:** Limited options? What does that even mean? I just need a little flexibility this month. I've been a customer for years.

**Lisa Wang:** I understand, Alex. My tools here mostly allow for standard payment extensions, usually up to seven days past the due date. For more structured payment plans, especially breaking a bill into multiple installments, that would require our dedicated Billing Solutions team. They have the specific tools and policies to review individual cases for extended payment options.

**Customer:** So you can't even give me a seven-day extension?

**Lisa Wang:** Let me check for that. (Typing) Yes, I could likely set up a standard seven-day extension, pushing your due date to May 8th. Would that be helpful for you, Alex?

**Customer:** (Sighs audibly) Seven days isn't really going to cut it, Lisa. I need more than that. I need to split this up. And honestly, it's really frustrating that I have to call multiple times for this. If my internet actually worked, I wouldn't be burning through data and then I wouldn't have this massive bill in the first place! This is like the fourth time I've called about a problem in the last month alone!

**Lisa Wang:** I truly apologize for the repeated issues and the inconvenience, Alex. I can see your service history here, and I understand why you're frustrated. I can definitely make a note of your persistent service concerns. What I can do on my end, immediately, is offer that seven-day extension. For anything beyond that, like a multi-part payment plan, I would need to transfer you directly to our Billing Solutions team. They are available until 6 PM PST today.

**Customer:** So, what, I get transferred and then I have to explain everything *again*?

**Lisa Wang:** I would make sure to include detailed notes on your account about your request for a payment arrangement and your ongoing service issues, so the next agent has that information. They'll be able to review your account history more thoroughly for those specific payment options.

**Customer:** (Quiet for a moment) Okay, fine. Can you transfer me then? And please make sure they know about all the internet problems too. I'm really close to just switching providers if this keeps up.

**Lisa Wang:** Absolutely, Alex. I'll make sure to document all your concerns, including your desire for a multi-part payment plan and the issues with your internet speed and mobile data overages. I'm transferring you now to our Billing Solutions team. Please stay on the line, and the next available agent will assist you. Just a moment, please.

**(Click and hold music starts for the customer)**

**Lisa Wang:** (To herself, after transferring) Okay, notes added. Hopefully, Billing can sort out the payment plan. And maybe a tech visit can actually fix his internet. Poor guy's got a lot of complaints.

**Call Transcript**

**Date:** 2025-01-31
**Time:** 10:47 AM EST
**Agent:** Jennifer Davis (agent_007) - Billing Specialist
**Customer ID:** C00050897
**Call Reason:** Customer questioning bill charges and payment issues.

---

**[00:00] Agent Jennifer Davis:** Thank you for calling TriLink Telecom, my name is Jennifer. How can I assist you today?

**[00:04] Customer (Mr. Henderson):** Hi Jennifer, yes, I need some help with my bill. I just got my statement for January, and it's… well, it’s completely wrong. It's showing $207. I'm used to paying around $167, and there’s a late fee on there too! What’s going on?

**[00:19] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I understand, sir. Let's take a look into that for you right away. To access your account, could I please get your full name and the phone number associated with your TriLink services?

**[00:28] Customer:** Sure, it's Michael Henderson, and my number is 555-401-8976.

**[00:35] Agent Jennifer Davis:** Thank you, Mr. Henderson. And just to confirm, for security, could you please provide your full billing address?

**[00:41] Customer:** It's 1409 Evergreen Lane, Springwood, PA 19008.

**[00:47] Agent Jennifer Davis:** Perfect, thank you. One moment while I pull up your account... Okay, I see your account here, Customer ID C00050897. You have our Standard 100 Mbps Internet and the Unlimited Standard Mobile plan for two lines. Is that correct?

**[01:03] Customer:** That’s right. And for those services, I usually pay about $167. I’ve been with TriLink for years, I know what my bill is usually.

**[01:12] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I see your current statement for January, showing a total of $207.00. Let me break down the charges for you.

**[01:19] Agent Jennifer Davis:** So, the Internet Standard_100 is listed at $64.00, and your Unlimited Standard Mobile plan for two lines is $118.00. That brings your recurring monthly total to $182.00.

**[01:34] Customer:** $182? But it’s always been less than that. For at least the last year it was around $167. What changed? And then there's that $25 late fee on top of it, making it $207.

**[01:46] Agent Jennifer Davis:** You're absolutely right to question that, Mr. Henderson. Looking back at your previous bills, I see that you had a "Bundle Savings" promotional discount of $15 applied to your account. This discount was for the first 12 months of your combined internet and mobile service.

**[02:04] Agent Jennifer Davis:** It appears that this promotional discount expired with your December bill cycle, meaning that for January, your services reverted to their standard combined price of $182.00 per month. This accounts for the increase from approximately $167 to $182.

**[02:22] Customer:** A promotion expired? Nobody told me that! I didn't get any notice it was ending. So, my bill just jumps up $15 without a word? That's not right.

**[02:30] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I do apologize if the notification wasn't clear, Mr. Henderson. Typically, the end date of promotional pricing is mentioned in the initial service agreement and sometimes on your monthly statement leading up to the expiry. However, I understand how frustrating it can be to see an unexpected increase.

**[02:47] Customer:** Frustrating is an understatement. And because of this surprise increase, I suppose that’s why there’s a $25 late fee? Because I was expecting $167 and maybe my payment for the December bill was short, or I just missed the higher amount?

**[02:59] Agent Jennifer Davis:** Yes, that's correct, Mr. Henderson. When the January bill was generated, the full amount of $182.00 was due on January 15th. Our records show that payment was not received for that full amount by the due date, leading to the $25 late payment charge applied to your current statement. It looks like a partial payment of $167 was received on January 20th.

**[03:22] Customer:** So you’re telling me because TriLink didn’t clearly inform me a discount was ending, my bill went up, and then because *I* didn't catch that, *I* got slapped with a $25 late fee? This is ridiculous, Jennifer. Can't you just reinstate the discount? Or at least waive this late fee?

**[03:39] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I completely understand your frustration, Mr. Henderson. Regarding the $15 Bundle Savings discount, it was a time-limited promotion, and unfortunately, I don't have the ability to reapply expired promotions directly from my end. Those are usually offered at the time of sign-up or during specific campaign periods.

**[04:00] Agent Jennifer Davis:** However, what I *can* do, given the confusion around the promotional expiry and the subsequent late fee, is offer a one-time courtesy waiver for that $25 late payment charge. I can process that for you right now, and you would see it reflected as a credit on your next bill.

**[04:20] Customer:** A one-time waiver for the late fee... so my bill will go back down to $182? That’s still $15 more than I was paying. I mean, it’s something, I guess. But I’m really not happy about this unannounced increase. Is there anything else you can do about the base $182 charge?

**[04:37] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I understand it's not the ideal solution you were hoping for, Mr. Henderson. While I can't reinstate the expired promotion, I can certainly review your account for any *new* bundle promotions or service plan adjustments that might help lower your monthly recurring charge closer to what you were paying before. Sometimes we have seasonal offers or loyalty discounts available for existing customers. Would you be interested in taking a few moments to go through those options with me? It wouldn't guarantee the same price, but we can explore what's available.

**[05:07] Customer:** Well, I'm already on the phone, so I suppose we can look. But honestly, I'm pretty annoyed right now. I just feel like this wasn't handled well by TriLink.

**[05:17] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I genuinely apologize for that experience, Mr. Henderson. Let's see what we can find for you. First, let me go ahead and process that $25 late fee waiver for you. It will show as a credit on your February bill. Does that sound good?

**[05:32] Customer:** Yes, please do that. And then let’s see what else you can dig up.

**[05:37] Agent Jennifer Davis:** Processing that now... Okay, that $25 credit has been applied to your account. You'll see it on your next statement. Now, regarding potential new offers...

**[05:48] Agent Jennifer Davis:** [Sound of typing/system navigation]

**[05:55] Agent Jennifer Davis:** Alright, Mr. Henderson, it looks like there aren't any direct, immediate loyalty promotions that would bring your current exact service package down by $15 right now. However, I see an option for upgrading your internet speed to our "Ultra_200" plan, which is 200 Mbps, for an additional $10 per month, and that comes with a new 6-month promotional discount of $5 off your mobile service. So, that would increase your internet, but net effect on mobile would save $5, leading to a new total of $187.00 for faster internet, plus the mobile discount. Or there's a mobile bundle with an additional line for $20 more, but that's probably not what you're looking for...

**[06:38] Customer:** So, if I upgrade my internet, my bill would be $187 instead of $182? That's *more* than what I'm paying now, and still significantly more than the $167 I was used to. And I don't need a faster internet speed, 100 Mbps is perfectly fine for me.

**[06:50] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I understand, Mr. Henderson. It seems our current promotional landscape doesn't quite align with finding a direct equivalent to your previous discount without altering your services significantly. Your current Internet_100 at $64 and Mobile Unlimited Standard at $118 are at their standard rates.

**[07:10] Customer:** So, basically, I'm stuck paying $182 now, and there’s nothing that can be done to get it back down to $167? No manager override, no special existing customer retention offer?

**[07:20] Agent Jennifer Davis:** Mr. Henderson, as a billing specialist, my tools allow me to see available promotions and make certain adjustments like the late fee waiver. For anything beyond that, like reinstating a past promotional rate, it would typically require review by a supervisor. I can certainly make a note on your account about your dissatisfaction with the promotional expiry and the new price point, and you could follow up with our customer retention department. They sometimes have different offers, but I can't guarantee any specific outcome for you.

**[07:54] Customer:** So you’re saying I’d have to call again? Another call, another explanation? I really don’t have time for this.

**[08:02] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I truly apologize for the inconvenience, Mr. Henderson. I understand your time is valuable. For now, I have waived that $25 late fee for you. Your next payment will be for the standard $182.00, less that $25 credit, making it $157.00. Beyond that, if you'd like to explore further options for a lower recurring monthly charge, speaking with our retention team would be the next step. I can provide you with their direct number and operating hours, or if you prefer, I can transfer you now, though there might be a hold time.

**[08:40] Customer:** (Sighs) No, don't transfer me now. I've spent enough time on this. Just make sure that late fee comes off. I'll think about whether I want to go through this whole song and dance again with another department. This is really poor customer service, Jennifer, not on your part, but TriLink's overall.

**[08:55] Agent Jennifer Davis:** I understand your frustration, Mr. Henderson. I've documented your feedback regarding the clarity of promotional expiry notifications and your desire to find a more competitive price point. The $25 late fee waiver is confirmed and will appear on your February bill. Is there anything else I can assist you with today regarding your account?

**[09:15] Customer:** No, that's all for now. Thank you, Jennifer.

**[09:19] Agent Jennifer Davis:** You're welcome, Mr. Henderson. Thank you for calling TriLink Telecom, and please have a good day.

**[09:23] Customer:** You too.

**[Call Ends]**

*(Typing sounds)*
Okay, I see you have our Premium_Gig internet plan, providing up to 1000 Mbps, for $100 a month. Is that correct?

**Customer Ms. Davies:** That's right. And for $100 a month, I expect it to work. We're a family of four, all working or studying from home, and this intermittent service is a nightmare. **Customer Ms. Davies:** Exactly! It's not just a one-off. This has been going on for weeks, becoming more frequent. I've tried all the basic stuff—rebooting the modem, checking cables. Nothing helps long-term.

**Agent Michael:** Alright. As a technical specialist, I'd like to perform some diagnostics from our end. First, can you tell me if your modem's lights are all solid, or are any blinking or showing an unusual color right now?

**Customer Ms. Davies:** Uh, let me look... Okay, the power light is solid green. The upstream and downstream lights are solid blue. The online light is also solid blue. But it's been doing that even when the internet is performing terribly.

**Agent Michael:** Thank you for checking that. That indicates the modem is registering a signal. Now, could you try a quick power cycle for me, just to ensure it's not a temporary cache issue? Please unplug your modem and your Wi-Fi router, if they are separate, for about 30 seconds, then plug them back in. We'll wait about two minutes for them to fully restart.

**Customer Ms. Davies:** *(Sighs audibly)* Michael, I just told you I've done this multiple times. It fixes it for maybe an hour, then it's back to the same old issues. But fine, I'll do it again.
*(Pause, sounds of movement)*
Okay, unplugged.

**Agent Michael:** Thank you for your patience, Ms. Davies. While that's restarting, I'm going to run a line test to your service address from my system.
*(Typing sounds, brief pause)*
Okay, I'm seeing your modem come back online now. Let me refresh these diagnostics.
*(Pause)*
Hmm. So, from my end, I'm seeing good signal levels coming into your modem *at this exact moment*. However, I am also seeing a history of intermittent upstream signal degradation that aligns with your previous reports, particularly on those outage dates. It looks like there are periods where the signal strength drops significantly, and then recovers. This suggests the issue isn't within your modem or router itself, but potentially further up the line, or perhaps even in the connection to your home.

**Customer Ms. Davies:** See? I knew it. It's not my equipment. So what are we going to do about it? This is just ridiculous for a premium service.

**Agent Michael:** You're absolutely right, and I apologize that you've been experiencing this ongoing inconsistency. Given the intermittent nature and the diagnostics indicating external factors, the most effective next step would be to schedule a technician visit. Our field technician can thoroughly test the line directly at your premises, check the external wiring, and investigate the connection point to the TriLink network to pinpoint the exact cause of these signal fluctuations.

**Customer Ms. Davies:** Another technician? Michael, this will be the third time in as many months someone's come out. The last guy said everything looked fine! And it was, for about a week. I can't keep taking time off work for this.

**Agent Michael:** I completely understand your frustration with needing multiple visits, Ms. Davies. I've made a detailed note of your service history, including the previous visits and the specific technical readings I'm seeing today, to ensure the dispatch team has all the information. This should help the technician on site perform a more targeted investigation. We aim to fix this permanently for you.

**Customer Ms. Davies:** What about a credit? I'm paying full price for 1000 Mbps, and I'm getting maybe 100 Mbps at best, with constant dropouts. It's false advertising at this point.

**Agent Michael:** I hear you, Ms. Davies. While I can't directly process a credit of that nature on this call, what I *can* do is make a strong recommendation on your account for a service credit due to these ongoing issues. Once the technician completes their visit and the underlying problem is resolved, our billing department reviews these recommendations. You can also follow up with us then, and we'll ensure it's processed fairly. The priority right now is getting the service stable.

**Customer Ms. Davies:** Fine. I need this fixed. What's the earliest a technician can come?

**Agent Michael:** Let me check the schedule for your area.
*(Typing sounds)*
Okay, it looks like the earliest availability for a technical specialist in your area, with the full diagnostic tools needed for this type of issue, would be this Saturday, June 15th, between 1 PM and 5 PM. Or, if that doesn't work, Monday, June 17th, between 9 AM and 1 PM.

**Customer Ms. Davies:** Saturday afternoon... Ugh. That's not ideal, but I guess it's better than Monday. Let's do Saturday, June 15th, 1 PM to 5 PM.

**Agent Michael:** Excellent. So that's confirmed: a TriLink technician will be at your address, C00077227, this Saturday, June 15th, between 1 PM and 5 PM. You'll receive a confirmation text message shortly with the appointment details. The technician will call you when they are approximately 30 minutes away. I've also added the detailed notes about the intermittent signal degradation and your past service issues, so they have the full picture.

**Customer Ms. Davies:** Alright. Please make sure they actually fix it this time. This can't keep happening.

**Agent Michael:** I completely understand, Ms. Davies, and I assure you we're committed to resolving this permanently. Your reference number for this call and the technician appointment is TRK-8854-3210. Is there anything else I can assist you with today, before the technician arrives?

**Customer Ms. Davies:** No, just get it fixed.

**Agent Michael:** I appreciate your patience and cooperation, Ms. Davies. Have a good rest of your day.

**Customer Ms. Davies:** You too.

**(Call Ends)**
